text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Friday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Finance Minister Robert Zile said there may be a 10-12 million lat budget deficit due to a tax shortfall.
- Central bank chief Einar Repshe said that the report of the working group investigating the loan transactions of Banka Baltiya and energy supplier Latvenergo had no teeth.
- Candidate Prime Minister Guntar Krasts said that the new government declaration may be approved on August 7. The post of culture minister is still not decided.
- From August 1 visa-free travel takes effect with Norway.
- The newspaper said its correspondent in Minsk, Igor Chertkov, was arrested during a rally of journalists against the arrest of journalist of Russian ORT Pavel Sheremeta.
- Potential investors of Latvenergo, German Preussen Elektra and Bewag, part of Ruhrgas, discussed the privatisation of the company with World Bank officials.
- A 25-metre high crane fell over in Riga but there were no casualties.
- An international conference on fighting money laundering will take place in Riga in May 1998.
- The central bank issued a list of 19 commercial banks which can accept individuals' deposits.

- A total 26 percent of Ventamonjaks, a chemical terminal in the port of Ventspils handling 12 kinds of bulk chemicals, will be sold, the privatisation agency ruled. It said that 35,010 shares of the company would be sold for 155 lats each.
